_note: Tagalog's paradigm is focus crossed with aspect: each verb has a completed, incompleted and contemplated form in every focus it takes. That grid is what the Gym exists to drill — it is the single hardest thing in the language and the most mechanical to practise.

entries.label: -um- actor focus
entries.usage: Actor is the topic.
entries.example: kain → kumain

entries.label: mag- actor focus
entries.usage: The other actor focus; pairs differ by root.
entries.example: luto → nagluto

entries.label: -in object focus
entries.usage: The thing acted on is the topic.
entries.example: kain → kinain

entries.label: -an locative focus
entries.usage: Place or recipient is the topic.
entries.example: bili → binilhan

entries.label: i- focus
entries.usage: Thing transferred or tool is the topic.
entries.example: bigay → ibinigay

entries.point: ma- and maka-: ability and the involuntary
entries.label: ma- / maka-
entries.usage: Ability, or something unintended.
entries.example: kita → nakita

entries.label: Causative
entries.usage: Have someone do it.
entries.example: luto → nagpaluto

entries.label: Reciprocal
entries.usage: To each other; joining in with.
entries.example: kita → magkita

entries.label: Choosing focus
entries.usage: The affix decides what is in view — a book, or the book.
entries.example: Bumili ako ng libro sa tindahan. — I bought a book at the store.

entries.label: Taglish affixes
entries.usage: Tagalog affixes go straight onto English roots — nag-drive, i-check.
entries.example: I-check mo ang email mo. — Check your email.

entries.label: Three aspects
entries.usage: Not tense — where the action stands.
entries.example: kumain / kumakain / kakain

entries.label: Recent perfective
entries.usage: Only just happened. Takes lang.
entries.example: kakakain lang

entries.label: ang pronouns
entries.usage: The topic slot.
entries.example: ako, ka, siya, tayo

entries.label: ng pronouns
entries.usage: Non-topic actor, and possessor.
entries.example: ko, mo, niya, namin

entries.label: sa pronouns
entries.usage: Direction, recipient, emphatic owner.
entries.example: akin, iyo, kaniya

entries.label: Deictics
entries.usage: Three degrees, by speaker and listener.
entries.example: ito / iyan / iyon

entries.label: ma- adjectives
entries.usage: Linker -ng after a vowel, na after a consonant.
entries.example: magandang bahay

entries.point: The ang phrase marks the sentence's topic
entries.label: ang marker
entries.usage: Marks the one thing the sentence is about.
entries.example: Kumain ang bata. — The child ate.

entries.point: ng marks a non-topic actor, object, or possessor
entries.label: ng marker
entries.usage: Marks the thing acted on, or the owner — anything that isn't what the sentence is about.
entries.example: Kumain ang bata ng pagkain. — The child ate (some) food.

entries.point: sa marks location, direction, or a specific place
entries.label: sa marker
entries.usage: Marks where something is, or where it is going.
entries.example: Pumunta ang bata sa bahay. — The child went to the house.

entries.label: Linker na
entries.usage: Joins a describing word to the thing it describes.
entries.example: Mabait na bata si Ana. — Ana is a kind child.

entries.label: mga plural
entries.usage: Goes before the noun to mean more than one.
entries.example: Naglalaro ang mga bata. — The children are playing.

entries.point: Existence and possession: may and wala
entries.label: may / wala
entries.usage: Say something exists or that you have it; wala is the no.
entries.example: May pagkain ako. — I have food.

entries.label: hindi negation
entries.usage: Goes right before the verb or adjective you are denying.
entries.example: Hindi kumain ang bata. — The child didn't eat.

entries.point: si and sina: names take their own marker
entries.label: si / sina
entries.usage: Names take si, never ang — sina for more than one.
entries.example: Kumain si Maria ng mangga. — Maria ate a mango.

entries.point: Questions: ba and the question words
entries.label: Questions
entries.usage: ba makes a yes/no question; ano, saan and bakit start the rest.
entries.example: Ano ang pangalan mo? — What is your name?

entries.label: Particle order
entries.usage: The little words stack in one fixed order — na before ba.
entries.example: Kumain na ba kayo? — Have you eaten already?

entries.label: ay inversion
entries.usage: Formal writing and speeches, with the topic moved to the front.
entries.example: Ang bahay ay maganda. — The house is beautiful.

entries.label: Comparison
entries.usage: When you set two things side by side, or pick out the one that beats all the rest.
entries.example: Mas mataas siya kaysa sa akin. — He is taller than me.

entries.label: Pseudo-verbs
entries.usage: Want, should, may — each takes a linker and a ng pronoun.
entries.example: Gusto kong matulog. — I want to sleep.

entries.label: mayroon
entries.usage: Use mayroon when a pronoun or particle comes between.
entries.example: Mayroon akong aso. — I have a dog.

entries.label: Numbers
entries.usage: Native numbers count things; Spanish ones do time and money.
entries.example: Bumili ako ng tatlong mangga. — I bought three mangoes.

entries.label: Nominalisation
entries.usage: Turn an action or a quality into a thing you can name.
entries.example: Mahalaga ang pag-aaral ng bata. — The child's studying is important.

entries.label: Relative clauses
entries.usage: When you need to say which one — the child who ate, the book you bought.
entries.example: Ang taong kumain ay umalis. — The person who ate left.

entries.label: Conditionals
entries.usage: If, whenever, and the wish that it were so.
entries.example: Kung umulan, hindi ako pupunta. — If it rains, I won't go.

entries.point: pang- instruments and other noun prefixes
entries.label: pang- / tag-
entries.usage: Names the tool you do it with, or the season.
entries.example: Ang panulat ay nasa mesa. — The pen is on the table.

entries.point: Register: Filipino, deep Tagalog, and Taglish
entries.label: Register
entries.usage: Choose between formal Filipino, deep Tagalog and everyday Taglish.
entries.example: Ang bata ay masipag mag-aral. — The child is diligent in studying.

entries.point: Aspect subtleties: na, pa, and the contemplated
entries.label: Already / still
entries.usage: na is already, pa is still, hindi pa is not yet.
entries.example: Kumakain pa siya. — He is still eating.

entries.label: Literary Filipino
entries.usage: For novels, news and speeches — not how anyone talks to a friend.
entries.example: Kay ganda ng umaga! — How beautiful the morning is!

entries.label: Frozen affixes
entries.usage: When a word looks built from a prefix and a root, learn it whole — the pieces no longer add up.
entries.example: Dalawa ang kapatid ko. — I have two siblings.
